summary: The bill requires the Treasury Secretary to designate the Council on American-Islamic Relations and all its chapters as Specially Designated Global Terrorists, which blocks their US assets, bans any transactions with them by US persons, adds them to the SDN list, and revokes their tax-exempt status.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to government spending, appropriations, or budgetary allocations. It focuses solely on terrorist designation and related sanctions.

Section 3(c) explicitly requires revocation of CAIR's 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status pursuant to IRC section 501(p). This removes a tax benefit for the designated entity and its affiliates, constituting a direct (though narrowly targeted) tax-related action rather than a broad tax policy change.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
No provisions address abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions affect military or defense spending levels.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.

The bill mandates terrorist designation, asset blocking, transaction prohibitions, and SDN listing for an organization alleged to have terrorism ties. This engages criminal justice by imposing stricter enforcement measures against entities supporting designated terrorist groups.
No provisions address trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions directly expand or limit legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid levels or programs.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address worker protections, unions, or employer flexibility.

The bill targets a Muslim-American civil rights organization for terrorist designation based on alleged Hamas links. While framed as national security, it directly impacts the legal and operational status of a religious-affiliated advocacy group, creating a tangential effect on religious liberty versus anti-discrimination balances.
